 K9 Vajra Howitzer: Features, Range, Indigenous Content and Defence Significance
 Learn about the K9 Vajra-T self-propelled howitzer, including its 155 mm gun, range, key features, L&T-Hanwha collaboration, indigenous content and India's defence modernisation for UPSC 2027.
 Posted by piyush Last updated on October 30th, 2026 12:48 pm 
 Leave a comment on K9 Vajra Howitzer: Features, Range, Indigenous Content and Defence Significance 
 Table of Contents
 Toggle Context 
 About K9 Vajra 
 Key Features 
 Context 
 The Ministry of Defence gave in-principle approval ( Acceptance of Necessity, AoN ) to buy 300+ more K9 Vajra-T self-propelled howitzers . The estimated cost is over ₹20,000 crore . 
 About K9 Vajra 
 Nature: A 155 mm, 52-calibre tracked self-propelled howitzer . It has an all-welded steel hull and good cross-country mobility. It is built for “shoot-and-scoot” strikes. 
 Manufacturer: Larsen & Toubro (L&T) , at its Armoured Systems Complex, Hazira, Gujarat . It works in technical collaboration with Hanwha Aerospace (South Korea) . 
 Aim: To give heavy, deep-strike fire support that moves with armoured columns, outranges enemy artillery and survives counter-battery fire . 
 Key Features 
 Range and Rate of Fire: Up to 40 km with standard high-explosive shells and up to 50 km with rocket-assisted shells. Fires 6–8 rounds a minute . 
 Shoot-and-Scoot: An automated fire control system and high mobility let it fire and move within minutes, avoiding counter-battery radar . 
 Protection: An all-welded steel hull and rotating turret protect against shell splinters, mines and small-arms fire . It can also pivot-turn . 
 Indigenous Content: Over 50% so far, including the fire control, autoloader and communication systems . The new batch needs over 70% domestic content. 
 Cold-Weather Upgrades: Auxiliary power units, heated battery compartments, special lubricants and winterisation kits for Himalayan heights above 14,000 feet .
